site.name: Apollo 17 lunar module (Taurus-Littrow valley)
site.coordinate_frame: Lunar mean Earth/polar axis (ME) system, as stated by the source; planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude. The source names no ephemeris realization; DE421 (as the DEM and Horizons MOON_ME) is assumed.
site.surface_elevation_reference: Height above the 1737.4 km sphere, SLDEM2015 512 px/deg tile sldem2015_512_00n_30n_000_045_float (LOLA + SELENE TC, Barker et al. 2016), bilinear at the published point interpreted in ME. Rounded to 0.1 m. LROC's table gives -2626 m from GLD100 (a different shape model; 2.0 m higher). See data/terrain/apollo17-lm_site_elevation_report.json.
site.horizons_altitude_reference: Height above the Horizons reference body for the Moon: a 1737.4 km sphere (response header 'Center radii'), the same reference as SLDEM2015 heights.
site.altitude_conversion_note: horizons_site_altitude_km = (surface_elevation_m + observer_height_above_surface_m) / 1000 = (-2628.0 m + 1 m) / 1000 = -2.627 km (negative: the site lies below the 1737.4 km sphere). Both heights are relative to the 1737.4 km sphere, so no datum conversion is needed. Rounding: the bilinear SLDEM2015 surface is -2627.9921 m; rounded to 0.1 m before forming the altitude, the submitted point is 0.9921 m above the interpolated surface (nominal 1 m). The generic terrain horizon and rendering use this same configured observer; no observer substitution is made.

sources.notes: Query parameters. Date consulted; time of day not recorded.

sources.title: JPL Horizons System Manual
sources.notes: Site coordinates on the Moon use the mean-Earth (DE421) frame with east-positive longitude; altitude is relative to the reference ellipsoid; after 1962 UT means UTC; no refraction for non-Earth sites. Date consulted; time of day not recorded.

position_conventions.azimuth: degrees clockwise from local north: N=0, E=90, S=180, W=270
position_conventions.elevation: degrees relative to the plane perpendicular to the reference-surface local zenith
position_conventions.apparent: airless apparent direction of target body center (light-time, gravitational deflection, stellar aberration)
position_conventions.time_scale: UTC (Horizons UT; after 1962 UT means UTC)
position_conventions.observer_body: Moon (301), MEAN_ME frame, east-longitude positive, reference sphere radius 1737.4 km
position_conventions.observer_altitude: site altitude above the 1737.4 km sphere = LOLA surface elevation + observer height above surface (see site.altitude_conversion_note)

horizon.processing_notes: Smooth-horizon approximation (Stage 1): 0 deg at every azimuth, i.e. the local horizontal plane of the reference-sphere observer. Terrain is NOT modeled; real local horizons near the lunar south pole can be several degrees high and would block low Sun/Earth directions.

Coordinate-driven coordinate-terrain-1. Airless body-centre visibility from one fixed observer; exact spherical curvature. Search extent: per-ray global-height stopping rule, bound 10873.0 m above 1737.4 km sphere. Source priority and bilinear valid-pixel selection from registry. No missing terrain replaced by zero. Radial and source-resolution limitations are in checks. Mesh never controls Horizon-view visibility.

products.name: sldem2015_512_00n_30n_000_045_float
products.nodata_rule: nonfinite or explicit sentinel is unknown; bilinear needs four valid pixels
products.registration: PDS/SLDEM label 1-based pixel centres; no half-pixel shift

setting_points.note: Terrain point setting each sampled skyline; shot counts not assessed by this generic path

radial_convergence.note: Every radial segment halved at 36 azimuths on the same DEM; not absolute terrain accuracy; first sample remains 5 m.

limitations: Source coordinates/frames retain their documented assumptions.
Global LDEM_64 is coarse distant terrain only; grid spacing varies with latitude. No fine obstacles are resolved.
No independent absolute terrain accuracy established. Source overlap statistics are differences, not accuracy estimates.
